examples: I listen to music in my room.
There is a bed in the room.
nuance: 방 is the general word for a room and also appears in compounds like 화장실 or 노래방.
mistakes: Using 에 instead of 에서 for an action done in the room.

examples: I wait in front of the door.
nuance: 문 covers doors and gates, and it joins words like 정문 for main gate.
mistakes: Saying 문이 열어요 instead of 문을 열어요 when you open it.

examples: There is a desk next to the window.
I look at the sky through the window.
nuance: 창문 is the everyday word for a window, while 창 alone is more literary or technical.
mistakes: Using 에 instead of 으로 for looking through the window.

examples: There is a bed in the room.
I read a book in bed.
I lie on the bed and rest.
nuance: 침대 means a Western style bed, and many Korean homes also use floor bedding called 이불.
mistakes: Using 에서 instead of 에 with the static verb 누워요.

examples: There is a chair in front of the desk.
There is a bag on the chair.
nuance: 의자 is any chair, and an office swivel chair is often called 사무용 의자.
mistakes: Saying 의자에서 앉아요 instead of 의자에 앉아요 for sitting down.

examples: There is a computer on the desk.
I do homework at the desk.
There are two desks in the room.
nuance: 책상 is a desk for studying or working, while a dining table is 식탁.
mistakes: Using 에 instead of 에서 when studying at the desk.

examples: I want to buy clothes at the department store.
nuance: 옷 takes the verb 입다 to wear, which differs from 신다 used for shoes on the feet.
mistakes: Saying 옷을 신어요 instead of 옷을 입어요 because 신다 is only for footwear.

examples: I take off my shoes in the house.
I want to put on new shoes.
nuance: 신발 takes the verb 신다 to wear, unlike 옷 which uses 입다 for the body.
mistakes: Saying 신발을 입어요 instead of 신발을 신어요 because 입다 is for clothing.

examples: There is a book inside the bag.
I want to buy a new bag.
There is a bag on the chair.
nuance: 가방 covers bags, backpacks, and handbags, and a backpack is also called 책가방 for school.
mistakes: Using 가방에 instead of 가방 안에 when you mean inside the bag.

examples: I watch movies on the computer.
There is a computer on the desk.
I turn on the computer and work.
nuance: 컴퓨터 is a loanword for a desktop or general computer, and a laptop is 노트북.
mistakes: Saying 컴퓨터에 일해요 instead of 컴퓨터로 일해요 for using it as a tool.

examples: I take photos with my cellphone.
I put the cellphone in the bag.
I want to buy a new cellphone.
nuance: 휴대폰 is the common word for a cellphone, and people also say 핸드폰 or simply 폰.
mistakes: Using 에 instead of 으로 when the phone is the means of calling.

examples: I open the door with the key.
There is a key in the bag.
nuance: 열쇠 is a physical key, while a digital door lock is usually called 도어록 or 번호키.
mistakes: Saying 열쇠에 문을 열어요 instead of 열쇠로 문을 열어요 for the tool.
